clue.text: See 15
See 15
Letters from Brother Aldhelm deceived goddess

indicators.note: only some consecutive letters are taken out of the words that follow, a run lifted from inside them

blocks.note: the run sits across the end of the first word and the start of the saint's name

explanation.surface: A monk named Aldhelm was tricked by a goddess, and his brother's letters tell the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence written by a monk, but it means alphabet letters lifted from the text: broTHER Aldhelm.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is queen of the Olympian deities in Greek myth, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Online space strange to M Roach

indicators.note: something strange is odd or out of its normal form, so these letters are put into an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written, the initial included

explanation.surface: Someone called M Roach finds the internet a baffling place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to M Roach' reads like a person's name with an initial, but its eight letters are the raw material, M included.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat room is a website area where users exchange messages live, a virtual meeting place on the internet.

clue.text: Something tiny Romeo wore outside

indicators.note: the clothing phrase goes on the outside, wrapped around the letter that comes before it

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
wore, as in had a garment on

explanation.surface: Romeo turns up wearing something very small on the outside, a skimpy costume perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wore' must be read as the two-word phrase 'had on', which then splits to wrap R: HAD-R-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A hadron is a subatomic particle such as a proton or neutron, as minute as matter gets.

clue.text: Tapestries restored where threads gradually removed?

indicators.note: restoration means putting back together, and here the letters are reassembled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Conservators restore old tapestries by pulling out worn threads one by one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'threads' the yarn in a wall-hanging; in the definition, threads is slang for clothes, taken off slowly. The question mark flags that playful twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is a performance where a dancer sheds clothing piece by piece, and threads is slang for garments.

clue.text: Parking in Asian metropolis for sacred site

indicators.note: one thing placed inside another, so a letter sits within the city's name

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the capital region of India

explanation.surface: Finding somewhere to park in a crowded Asian city is a quest worthy of a pilgrim.
explanation.walkthrough: The P slips into Delhi between L and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi in ancient Greece was the shrine of Apollo and home of its famous oracle, a holy place.

clue.text: Lead removed from silver say and elsewhere

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, and removing it leaves the rest

blocks.note: silver is an example of a metal, signalled by 'say'

explanation.surface: Lead is extracted from silver ore here and in other places too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' and 'silver' look like two metals in a refining story; lead is actually the first letter. Et al can abbreviate Latin et alibi as well as et alii.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al abbreviates the Latin et alibi, meaning in other places, used in references to point further afield.

clue.text: Senseless how burlesque ends

indicators.note: where a word ends is its final letter, so only that one letter is kept

blocks.note: how something ends is told as 'in a' or 'in an' followed by what it ends in
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A comment that burlesque shows always finish in some pointless way.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay describes the spelling of burlesque, not the show: its final letter is E, so it ends IN AN E.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly, lacking meaning or intelligence, the same as pointless or foolish.

clue.text: Explosive material about creativity sincere

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pair of pieces goes round the next

blocks.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
a matted woollen fabric
art is creative skill

explanation.surface: Someone's creative work is explosive stuff, and they mean it sincerely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive material' reads as one thing, like gelignite, but it splits into two pieces that then wrap round the creativity.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartfelt feelings come from deep within, genuine and earnest rather than put on.

clue.text: Crouchback for one thrown in road by king

indicators.note: a word meaning inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: a lane is a narrow road
to cast is to throw
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A hunchbacked man is flung into the road beside a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Crouchback was the first Earl of Lancaster, son of Henry III; 'for one' marks him as an example of a holder of that name or title.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Crouchback founded the royal House of Lancaster as its first earl, so he is one example.

clue.text: Mischievous duo taking female out for drive

indicators.note: here taking something out removes it, so a letter is lost

blocks.note: two mischievous little creatures, an imp and an elf
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A pair of pranksters take a woman out for a spin in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking female out for drive' reads as a date in a car; the woman is just F, removed from the second sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to urge or push forward, the same sense as to drive someone to act.

clue.text: Look after book for Welsh entertainer

blocks.note: a novel is a book
lo is an old word for look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to mind a book on behalf of a Welsh performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' reads as a phrasal verb meaning to care for, but 'after' just places the look piece behind the book piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a Welsh composer, actor and songwriter, a star of stage and screen.

clue.text: Husband in delicate position

indicators.note: one thing inside another, so a letter sits within the adjective

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
nice can mean subtle or finely balanced, as in a nice distinction

explanation.surface: A husband finds himself in an awkward spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delicate position' reads as a tricky situation, but the definition is position alone; nice in its older sense means fine or delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a comfortable or suitable role or place, a particular position one fills.

clue.text: Room for experimentation in party rhetoric

blocks.note: Lab is short for Labour, the British political party
oratory is the art of persuasive public speaking

explanation.surface: A party's speeches leave space for trying out new ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Lab is the standard short form for the UK Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a workplace equipped for scientific tests and research.

clue.text: Four in romcom linked with sexual celebration

indicators.note: one thing placed within another, so the numeral sits inside the adjective

blocks.note: the 1999 romantic comedy starring Hugh Grant and Julia Roberts
IV is four in Roman numerals
carnal means relating to physical, sexual desire

explanation.surface: A romantic comedy foursome gets mixed up in a racy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four in romcom' suggests Four Weddings and a Funeral, another Hugh Grant film, but four belongs with 'sexual'. Notting Hill is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Notting Hill Carnival is a huge Caribbean street festival held in west London every August bank holiday.

clue.text: Good boy receiving new organ

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so one piece holds a letter within it

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a lad is a boy
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A well-behaved boy gets a transplant or perhaps a new instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' could be the church instrument the good boy is given; it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland is a bodily organ that secretes substances such as hormones.

clue.text: Tabloid target in Sulawesi — French are leaving

indicators.note: whatever is leaving goes away, so those letters drop out

blocks.note: The former name of this Indonesian island
es is the French for 'are', as in tu es

explanation.surface: A tabloid's quarry hides out in Indonesia as the French move out.
explanation.walkthrough: Sulawesi was long known in English as Celebes; dropping the French word for 'are' from its end leaves the short form of celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeb, short for celebrity, is a famous person whom gossip papers chase for stories.

clue.text: Cheeky Girl shunning any number to be sociable?

indicators.note: to shun is to avoid, so a letter is kept out of the word

blocks.note: a minx is an impudent, cheeky girl
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: One of the Cheeky Girls, the 2000s pop duo, refuses to join in with the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals point to the Cheeky Girls pop act, but it is just an impudent girl. The question mark flags that the definition is a loose sense of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix is to socialise or mingle with other people at a gathering.

clue.text: Times Cryptic Hotline gives 'rock fragment'

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the following letters are scrambled into a riddle

blocks.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper's puzzle helpline supplies a solver with a geology answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Times the newspaper, with its famous cryptic crossword; in fact it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A xenolith is a foreign piece of rock embedded within igneous rock of a different kind.

clue.text: Charm gypsy man among reformed drinkers

indicators.note: to be among others is to be surrounded by them, so one piece goes within

blocks.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, the group for recovering drinkers
a Rom is a Romani man

explanation.surface: A traveller charms a gathering of former alcoholics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like a verb, as in a fortune teller beguiling the crowd, but it is a noun: an appealing quality.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma can mean a pervasive, attractive quality or atmosphere, much like a subtle allure.

clue.text: State in which goodish priest keeps house

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so this piece holds another within

blocks.note: OK means acceptable, fairly good
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A decent clergyman runs a household somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State in which' reads as a condition; it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the fifty American states, in the south central region.

clue.text: Back where witch lived — she heartless

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is cut out

blocks.note: the Witch of Endor appears in the Old Testament book of Samuel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cruel woman returns to the place where a witch once lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a direction or return, but it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to support it publicly, the same as to back it.

clue.text: Limb found in river and well

indicators.note: something found in a place lies within it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A severed arm is discovered in a river and down a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a water source alongside the river, but it is the interjection of mild surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or dismay, interjections said when something unexpected happens.

clue.text: Horse one Queen maltreated

definitions.note: a noun used attributively, as in horse racing, matching the adjective

indicators.note: to maltreat is to handle roughly, so the letters are knocked out of shape

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch's horse is badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' must become the numeral, not the word, or there are too many letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means relating to or resembling horses, so it stands for horse used as a modifier.

clue.text: Dander raised, wanted to strangle learner driver

indicators.note: strangling means gripping round the neck, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: to want is to need
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: Someone is so furious they want to throttle the person taking driving lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: To get one's dander up is to become angry; British learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means irritated or provoked, the state of having one's temper roused.

clue.text: American devoured by worst animal

indicators.note: whatever is devoured ends up inside the eater, so one letter goes within

blocks.note: to worst someone is to beat them, as is to best them
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A tourist from the States is eaten by the most terrible creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' looks like the superlative of bad, but it is the verb meaning defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature, especially a large or wild four-legged one.

clue.text: One called 11 baronet encircling old city

indicators.note: encircling something means surrounding it, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: Bt is the abbreviation for baronet
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A titled nobleman surrounds an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 points to the answer at 11-across: the Hollywood actor Burt Lancaster had that surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Burt Lancaster, the American film star, bore the surname given at 11, so he was a person so called.

clue.text: Use handle wrongly — let go

indicators.note: doing something wrongly means not in the right way, so the letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions on misusing a handle, ending with the advice to let go of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let go' fits a hand on a handle in the surface, but here it is a past participle meaning released.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleashed means released from restraint, freed like a dog off its lead.

clue.text: Deadly reptiles spring up to claim son

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read from bottom to top
to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Venomous snakes leap up and seize a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring up' reads as leap, but spring is the noun for a water source; up turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are venomous snakes, the Egyptian cobra famously associated with Cleopatra.

clue.text: Many a Welsh runner in the gloaming

blocks.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, standing for a large number
the Usk is a river in south Wales, and a river runs

explanation.surface: Plenty of Welsh joggers come out for an evening run as night falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' means a river, a crossword favourite; the Usk flows through south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloaming is a Scottish word for twilight, the darkening time just after sunset.

clue.text: Painting class in new term

indicators.note: something new has been made afresh, so the letters are remade in another order
one piece placed inside another, so a word sits within the reworked letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a brand is a kind or class of thing

explanation.surface: An art class is starting up in the new school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painting class' looks like an art lesson; painting is the definition, and a Rembrandt is a canvas by the Dutch master.
explanation.definitionFit: A work by the Dutch artist can be named after its painter, so a Rembrandt is one of his canvases.

clue.text: Repeatedly questions MP involved in discharge

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up within it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: pus is the fluid discharged from an infection
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician caught up in a scandal is grilled again and again before being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests dismissal from a job; it is the medical sense. An MP is a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to interrogate them persistently for information.
